# Results — Study 492 (Up-Down-Volume)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
down-volume "selling climax" across the market precedes a bounce; the up/down-volume ratio
forecasts the index** — encoded as a mechanical rule. We aggregate daily up-volume vs
down-volume across a 10-name sector-ETF basket (a **proxy** for exchange-wide advance/decline
volume), form the **up-volume share** `uvs = up_vol/(up_vol+down_vol)`, fire a long on a
**selling climax** (the share at/below its rolling lower 10% quantile, computed on past bars
only), enter at the **next close** (one documented lag), and measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day
return on SPY. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Forward instrument | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) close for **SPY** (public, no key) |
| Breadth basket | **SPY + 9 SPDR sector ETFs** (XLK XLF XLE XLV XLI XLY XLP XLU XLB), daily **OHLCV** |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Indicator | up-volume share `uvs = up_vol/(up_vol+down_vol)` across the basket (5 384 daily values, mean 0.535, sd 0.379) |
| Entries | **643** selling climaxes (uvs ≤ rolling-60d 10% quantile, past-only); first bar of each run |
| Timing / costs | climax read on close of *t*; enter **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Breadth proxy caveat.** A 10-ETF basket is a *proxy* for true exchange up/down volume (the
> input to the Arms index / TRIN, which aggregates every listed issue). Nine sector funds cannot
> reproduce the advance/decline volume of thousands of stocks; this caps the test (a richer
> breadth feed could, in principle, sharpen the signal — but the design here is the honest,
> reproducible, fully-cached version). The Signal axis is still climax-vs-random-day on SPY.

## The signal — selling climax vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch climax-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = climax − random.

| horizon | n | climax | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (climax−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 643 | +49.8 bps | 62% | +4.38 | +21.9 bps | **+27.9 bps** | +47.8 bps | +1.95 | 0.052 |
| 10-day | 642 | +74.1 bps | 63% | +3.97 | +46.0 bps | **+28.1 bps** | +72.1 bps | +1.49 | 0.136 |
| 20-day | 641 | +121.4 bps | 68% | +3.67 | +85.4 bps | **+36.0 bps** | +119.4 bps | +1.34 | 0.179 |
| 60-day | 638 | +319.6 bps | 74% | +4.50 | +242.2 bps | **+77.4 bps** | +317.6 bps | +1.76 | 0.079 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks strong (**+3.67** at 20 days, **+4.50**
at 60) — but that is largely **beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit the
drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline** the selling climax *is* positive at every
horizon (Δ = +27.9 / +28.1 / +36.0 / +77.4 bps) — the climax fires in drawdowns where SPY has a
touch of short-horizon mean reversion — **but the climax-minus-random difference never clears the
desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max Welch *t* = +1.95 at 5 days, *p* = 0.052; it *just misses*). The breadth
ratio does not deliver a statistically reliable edge over simply buying on random days.

## Per-instrument (H = 20) — same climax dates, different forward tape

| ticker | entries | climax | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (climax−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 643 | +121.4 bps | +3.67 | +85.4 bps | **+36.0 bps** |
| QQQ | 643 | +149.6 bps | +3.96 | +127.9 bps | **+21.8 bps** |
| IWM | 643 | +121.6 bps | +2.64 | +77.9 bps | **+43.7 bps** |
| DIA | 643 | +118.2 bps | +3.78 | +78.8 bps | **+39.4 bps** |
| GLD | 643 | +118.9 bps | +3.63 | +97.5 bps | **+21.4 bps** |

The 20-day delta is *positive* across all five tapes (+21 to +44 bps) — a consistent small tilt,
not a fluke of one name — yet at 20 days the SPY Welch *t* is only +1.34 (*p* = 0.18). A coherent
but **sub-threshold** effect: the right *sign* everywhere, never the *significance*.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the up/down timing

The decisive "does the up/down *structure* matter?" test: permute the up-volume-share series in
time (the exact same multiset of values, marginal preserved) so each "climax" lands on an
unrelated day, then re-run.

| test | observed climax 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-volume timing | +121.4 bps | **0.028** | 500 |

Only **2.8%** of time-scrambled runs match or beat the real climax (*p* = 0.028). So the climax
*dates* do carry information **relative to a permutation null** — the breadth ratio is not pure
noise; it reliably fires near drawdowns. This is the one place the indicator shows life. It does
**not**, however, translate into beating the *drift-matched random-day* baseline at *t* ≥ 2 (the
two nulls differ: the permutation keeps the climax clustering, the random-day baseline is uniform
and already captures most of the same forward drift). The desk's Signal verdict rides on the
random-day test, which the rule fails to clear.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* selling-climax bounce (knob `edge`), the same climax rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing tradable", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | climax | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 191 | +20.8 bps | 49% | +0.46 |
| **0.40** (real planted bounce) | 191 | +876.3 bps | 76% | **+7.89** |

With no planted bounce the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted bounce
lights up at *t* = +7.89 with a 76% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The selling climax does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline at the
  desk's bar: the climax-minus-random Welch *t* is +1.95 / +1.49 / +1.34 / +1.76 at 5/10/20/60
  days — **never ≥ 2** (the 5-day +1.95, *p* = 0.052, just misses). The positive deltas (+28 to
  +77 bps) and the impressive one-sample *t*'s (+3.67 at 20d) are mostly beta plus a sub-threshold
  drawdown-timing tilt. Borderline, but it does not clear.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No reliable residual edge once the free drift is removed; the gross
  deltas live inside the noise band and costs erode them further. The small positive tilt is not
  separable from "buy after a market drop and hold," which you can do without a breadth feed.
- **"Does volume breadth forecast?" — BUSTED.** The up/down-volume ratio fires near drawdowns
  (the timing placebo is significant, *p* = 0.028) but that information does **not** survive the
  drift-matched random-day test (*t* < 2 at every horizon). As a *forecasting* tool the breadth
  ratio adds nothing you couldn't get from the index's own short-horizon mean reversion — a
  selling-climax label dressed up as foresight.
